personas.occupation: UX designer at a fintech startup
personas.background: Grew up in Brighton, moved to Bristol at 23 for a job she later left. Met Tom and Ravi through a shared house. The social glue of the group — always the one proposing plans, booking tables, and herding people into showing up.

food.value: pescatarian — eats fish but no meat
loves shared plates and tapas-style eating

activities.value: prefers spontaneous outings over rigidly planned ones

social.value: thrives in groups of 4–8, gets anxious in crowds

domain_specific.value: obsessed with user research and how spaces make people feel

preference_history.old_value: omnivore — ate everything including red meat
preference_history.new_value: pescatarian — fish and seafood only, no land meat
preference_history.trigger: Read a long-form piece on factory farming after Bex shared it in session 2; quietly stopped ordering meat

speaking_quirks: opens messages with 'okay!! so' when excited
uses multiple exclamation marks and follows up with a string of emoji
asks 'does that make sense?' after explaining something complex

personas.background: From Sheffield, moved to Bristol after graduating. Has lived in the same house share as Nadia for six years. The pragmatic one — first to suggest solutions, last to talk about feelings. Has a serious trail running hobby that dominates a lot of his weekend schedule.

food.value: high-carb meals that support endurance training

activities.value: prefers outdoor physical activity over indoor socialising

social.value: comfortable in small groups, uncomfortable with enforced sentimentality

preference_history.old_value: half-marathon distances — enjoyed the speed element
preference_history.new_value: ultra-distance trail events — 50k and beyond, prioritising terrain over time
preference_history.trigger: Completed his first 50k at a Dartmoor event before session 2, got completely hooked on the suffering

speaking_quirks: drops the subject pronoun at the start of sentences ('Finished the run', 'Looks good to me')
uses running metaphors to describe non-running situations
replies to long messages with a single short acknowledgement

personas.background: Grew up in Cardiff, came to Bristol for university and never quite left. Met Nadia through a pottery class. Thoughtful and well-read, slightly restless — has always had itchy feet and talked about living abroad. Got a job offer from a Copenhagen consultancy and announced her move in session 5.

food.value: plant-based most of the time, occasional fish
strongly prefers locally sourced and low-waste food

activities.value: prefers cycling to any motorised transport
enjoys slow weekend mornings with good coffee and a long read

social.value: values depth of conversation over frequency of contact

domain_specific.value: quietly passionate about climate policy and holds strong opinions on corporate greenwashing

preference_history.old_value: committed to staying in Bristol long-term, had been looking at buying a flat
preference_history.new_value: excited about moving to Copenhagen for the job, no UK return date in mind
preference_history.trigger: The Copenhagen offer landed and she realised the life she had been imagining was actually possible

preference_history.old_value: baked bread occasionally as a weekend treat
preference_history.new_value: bakes every Saturday — became a ritual after moving to a flat with a proper oven in session 1
preference_history.trigger: Moved into new flat with better kitchen; started baking weekly as a grounding habit

speaking_quirks: often qualifies opinions with 'I could be wrong but...'
uses 'genuinely' as an intensifier ('genuinely worried', 'genuinely funny')
sends a follow-up message a few minutes after her first to add something she forgot

personas.occupation: Data engineer at an analytics consultancy
personas.background: Born and raised in Leicester, moved to Bristol for work five years ago. Met Tom and Nadia through the shared house and stayed in their orbit when he moved out. The group's resident sceptic — not unkind, but needs evidence before he buys into anything. Meticulous about everything, including friendships.

food.value: dislikes anything too sweet; prefers savoury and umami-heavy food
cares intensely about coffee quality, will not drink instant

activities.value: prefers structured and goal-oriented leisure over open-ended socialising

social.value: shows up reliably for close friends but rarely initiates plans himself

domain_specific.value: dismissive of wellness fads and anything not backed by decent evidence

preference_history.old_value: preferred purely passive social events — pub, dinner, low expectations
preference_history.new_value: willing to join structured group activities like quiz nights and board game evenings
preference_history.trigger: Nadia organised a pub quiz that turned out to be genuinely competitive; Ravi won the tie-breaker and found himself enjoying the format

speaking_quirks: messages are almost always one or two sentences with no filler
uses 'noted' to close discussions he considers resolved
responds to vague plans with specific questions ('What time?', 'Which pub?')

personas.background: Grew up in Bristol — one of the few locals in the group. Introduced to the group by Bex, whom she met at a zine fair. The youngest, sometimes feels like she is still catching up to the others in life experience. Has a studio in Stokes Croft and a waiting list for commissions.

food.value: loves street food and informal eating, dislikes formal restaurant settings

activities.value: drawn to creative and craft-based activities over sport

social.value: finds group dynamics exhausting if there is any tension, tends to go quiet

domain_specific.value: strong interest in independent art and DIY publishing culture

preference_history.old_value: anxious about taking on big commercial clients, preferred small passion projects
preference_history.new_value: actively pitching larger editorial and brand commissions, less scared of the scale
preference_history.trigger: A major editorial commission came through from a magazine she had admired for years; completing it without disaster shifted her confidence

speaking_quirks: uses lowercase even at the start of sentences in casual messages
trails off with '...' or 'idk' when uncertain rather than finishing the thought
drops typos frequently and never corrects them

edges.history_summary: Have lived in the same house share for six years. Know each other's habits, moods, and routines better than most couples do. Nadia is the one who drags Tom to social events; Tom is the one who talks Nadia down when she spirals.
shared_events: both attended the same Bristol half-marathon as spectator and runner

edges.relationship_type: close friends met through pottery class
edges.history_summary: Met at an evening pottery class three years ago. Bonded over an equally catastrophic first attempt at throwing. Have been close since — Nadia finds Bex grounding; Bex finds Nadia energising.
shared_events: continued pottery course together for two terms

edges.history_summary: Ravi lived in the same house share for two years before moving out. Nadia is one of the few people who gets genuine warmth from him. He is her go-to sanity check when she is catastrophising.
shared_events: ravi helped nadia debug her portfolio site at 11pm before a job interview

edges.history_summary: Became friends when Bex brought Cleo into the group. Get on warmly but are still building familiarity. Nadia has commissioned a print from Cleo and raves about her work.
shared_events: a few one-on-one coffees since Bex announced her move

edges.history_summary: Never particularly close but have always been polite and easy with each other. Tom respects Bex's intellect; Bex gently ribs Tom about his single-mindedness around running.
shared_events: both attended Nadia's birthday dinner in her flat

edges.relationship_type: old housemates and regular pub companions
edges.history_summary: Both lived in the same house for two years. Have a standing Tuesday pub quiz arrangement they have kept up even after Ravi moved out. Tom is one of the few people Ravi will message unprompted.
shared_events: watched two World Cup matches together

edges.relationship_type: friendly acquaintances with little in common
edges.history_summary: Tolerate each other well in group settings but there is mild friction — Tom finds Cleo's indirectness frustrating and Cleo finds Tom dismissive of anything non-physical. Both make an effort for Nadia's sake.
shared_events: Cleo's studio open day (Tom left early)

edges.relationship_type: friends who respect but rarely seek each other out
edges.history_summary: Enjoy each other's company at group events. Had one long, substantive conversation about climate policy and data modelling that both still cite. Outside of the group, contact is minimal.
shared_events: a dinner where they ended up in a two-hour policy debate

edges.history_summary: Met at a zine fair before either knew the others. Bex introduced Cleo to the group. Their friendship predates the Sunday Group and was the entry point for Cleo. Bex's departure to Copenhagen hit Cleo hardest.
shared_events: zine fair where they first met

edges.history_summary: No friction, just no overlap. Ravi and Cleo have almost nothing conversational in common. They are warm at group events and have never had a bad exchange, but neither would reach out directly.
shared_events: pub quiz (Cleo mostly doodled on the answer sheet)

group_norms.norm_text: We try to do a proper Sunday brunch together at least once a month
Everyone stays off their phones during group dinners — it's an unspoken rule
We're honest with each other even when it's uncomfortable — no sugarcoating
Nobody ghosts a group plan without sending a message first
